page.title: In the browser
page.description: Run tinyactors in a page, a Worker, Node.js or Bun with @tinyactors/wasm: the same API as @tinyactors/node, with core compiled to WebAssembly.

hero.headline: Run the same API in a browser.
hero.lede: @tinyactors/wasm is the API of @tinyactors/node with core compiled to WebAssembly. It runs in a page, in a Worker, and in Node.js and Bun on a platform with no addon, such as Windows.

section.heading: Only the import changes.
section.p: Every other guide holds for this package, with the same names, shapes and errors. This program logs the same line from a page as from Node.js:

section.heading: Import it, or load it with init().
section.p: The package's entry loads its module, tinyactors.wasm beside its files, with top-level await. Every name works once the import settles.
A browser loads it with fetch and WebAssembly.compileStreaming, and Node.js and Bun read the file.
A Service Worker refuses a module graph with top-level await. Some bundlers neither handle it nor place tinyactors.wasm beside the bundle: esbuild does not follow new URL(..., import.meta.url).
For them, @tinyactors/wasm/init exports the same names and init(source?), which loads the module once. Until it settles, every call throws TA_ERROR_STATE.
source is a URL, a Response, the bytes or a compiled WebAssembly.Module. Without one, init loads the package's own file.

example.code: before init: TA_ERROR_STATE after init: closed false

section.p: The package targets ES2022 and serves the module as @tinyactors/wasm/tinyactors.wasm, so a bundler or a CDN can place it.

section.heading: Chrome 114, Firefox 119, Safari 16.4 run it.
section.p: The module uses WebAssembly's extended-const, multivalue, bulk-memory and nontrapping-fptoint. The package uses top-level await and String.prototype.isWellFormed.
By the engines' release notes, that means Chrome and Edge 114, Firefox 119 and Safari 16.4. Only Chromium 141 is tested.

section.heading: Allow 'wasm-unsafe-eval', and 'unsafe-eval' for native.
section.p: The module needs 'wasm-unsafe-eval' in script-src. The native datamodel evaluates your charts' expressions and scripts as JavaScript, so it needs 'unsafe-eval' too.
Three policies make new Host(...) on the native datamodel throw TinyactorsError with TA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED, its message naming the directive:

item.text: Trusted Types enforced (require-trusted-types-for 'script'), which guards string evaluation even with 'unsafe-eval'.

section.p: Under them, compileCharts skips its check of the charts' JavaScript syntax, since it parses with the same constructor. Such a page runs its charts on quickjs.

section.heading: Bytes are Uint8Arrays on both packages.
section.p: What a host hands out as bytes is a Uint8Array: compiled.image, host.hibernate(), host.snapshot(), host.metrics(), telemetry and encode().

@tinyactors/node gives Buffers, a subclass of Uint8Array, so code written against Uint8Array runs on both. Decode text with TextDecoder, not buf.toString(), and compare or copy with the typed array's own methods.
index.d.ts, which both packages share, says Uint8Array everywhere.

section.heading: quickjs needs only 'wasm-unsafe-eval'.
section.p: datamodel: 'quickjs' runs the charts on quickjs-ng inside the package's module. It has the same limits, realms, hibernation, migration and snapshots as in @tinyactors/node ().
quickjs evaluates no chart text with your engine. It is the datamodel for a page whose policy forbids 'unsafe-eval', and for charts you do not trust.
Every page downloads quickjs in the one module: 378 KiB with brotli, against 137 KiB without quickjs. mise run pack:wasm reports the sizes.
Its engine's stack is the module's, at most 256 KiB whatever quickjs.stackLimit asks. A deeper recursion is its evaluation's error.execution, RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
Its Date reads the real clock, as in @tinyactors/node, whatever clock the host runs on.

section.heading: Charts run in the host's own realm.
section.p: Chart code is trusted code here too: it runs in your engine, not in a sandbox. Its realm is the host's own, made at its first chart.

row.cell: a hidden iframe of the page's origin, one per host, removed at close()
the worker's own global (a Worker has no document)

section.p: Each session is a scope object in that realm. A script's top-level declarations mean what they mean in @tinyactors/node (Writing charts):

item.text: a chart-level script's functions are the chart's helpers, made once;
a top-level var is a variable of the session;
let, const and class at a script's top level are refused.

section.p: Scripts and expressions run as strict code. An assignment to a name nobody declared is the script's error.execution, never a variable of the realm.

section.heading: Give the charts a Worker of their own.
section.p: On a page the charts share the page's thread, so a long macrostep is a frame the page does not draw.
In a dedicated Worker the page stays responsive, and the charts' realm holds none of the page's code. Only values cross postMessage, as between any two systems.
The page waits for the worker to say it listens, since a message sent before the worker's module ran is lost:
The worker, counters-worker.mjs beside the page, answers each question through an I/O processor once its host is idle:
A module Worker has no import map. A bundler resolves @tinyactors/wasm in the worker as in the page, or the worker imports the package's index.mjs by its URL.

section.heading: Keep hibernated actors in IndexedDB.
section.p: The host does no I/O in a browser either, so where hibernated actors and snapshots live is yours. A browser has no SQLite and refuses SQLiteStore ().
A page has IndexedDB, which stores a Uint8Array as it is. A store's methods may return promises, which the host follows, so IndexedDB serves as a host's store directly.
This counter is hibernated into IndexedDB, and loaded from it when its next event comes:

section.heading: Timers come late in a hidden tab.
section.p: In Node.js an open host with a pending deadline keeps the process alive. A page has no such process: its hosts run while the page does.
A host runs its turns as MessageChannel messages and arms one setTimeout at its next deadline.
A browser throttles a hidden tab's timers. Chromium runs them about once a second, and once a minute after a few minutes hidden.
A delayed <send> or a timeout then comes late, but is never lost: it runs when the timer fires. A dedicated Worker is throttled less, but is not exempt.

section.heading: Snapshot the host when the page hides.
section.p: A tab can be closed, discarded or frozen without notice, and its actors go with it. Keep what must survive in your store.
Hibernate actors as they go cold, or snapshot the host on visibilitychange, the last event a page is sure to get. Restore it when the page loads again.
This cart is snapshotted into IndexedDB, then restored by a second load with its item kept:
A snapshot leaves out the services your program runs, which a restore announces again ().

section.heading: WebAssembly memory grows and never shrinks.
section.p: The host's memory is the module's linear memory, which is never given back: a page keeps its peak.

item.term: Hibernation makes room, not a smaller page.
item.text: Hibernating actors frees room for others in that memory. A snapshot is packed there before it is copied out, so a 100 MB snapshot leaves the memory 100 MB larger.
wasm32 addresses 4 GiB, and a region that grows is copied before the old one is freed. So one host holds about two million resident actors at most, where @tinyactors/node goes on.

item.term: What the package hands out stays valid.
item.text: Bytes, values and views are never views of that memory, so they stay valid when it grows.

section.p: Capacity and memory gives what an actor costs.

section.heading: Values cross between packages, snapshots do not.
section.p: A server on @tinyactors/node and a browser client on @tinyactors/wasm can share a database. They cannot share the bytes a host packs.

item.text: It is the host's memory as the build that made it lays it out, and the addon is a 64-bit build where the module is a 32-bit one. Each package labels its snapshots with its own name and refuses the other's with TA_ERROR_INVALID, the message naming the package that made it.

item.term: A hibernation blob belongs to its host.
item.text: It wakes in the host that hibernated it, or in one restored from that host's snapshot, which the other package cannot restore; another host's blob throws TA_ERROR_INVALID. Keep the server's blobs and the client's apart in the store, by host.
encode and decode are one format in both packages (): move work between the server and the client as events and their data, from one system to another.
